author: David Wilson
title: Noem Rips Sanctuary City Over ICE Detainer Compliance - NewsBreak
text: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem has sharply criticized Chicago’s sanctuary city policies, claiming that local authorities routinely reject the majority of ICE detainer requests. A DHS report noted that detainer compliance in Chicago has remained low, fueling federal concerns over public safety and immigration enforcement. Illinois Democrats defended the city’s stance, arguing that the policies align with state law. Noem said, “In just the last seven months, ICE has issued over 1,664 detainers in Chicago alone.” She added, “Unfortunately, Chicago and its leadership has only honored 8% of those.” Noem said, “The elected leaders in this state of Illinois are ignoring the law. In fact, they’re being obstructionists when it comes to getting dangerous criminals off their streets.” DHS cited data showing that only 8% of ICE detainers have been honored in Chicago. Noem claimed the policy led to releases after local arrests. Noem said the alleged “obstructionists” include “Governor [JB] Pritzker, Mayor [Brandon] Johnson, and others who have worked so hard to protect these dangerous criminals. They’d rather be a sanctuary state and continue to put those individuals above American citizens.” The Justice Department published a list naming Illinois, Cook County, and Chicago as sanctuary jurisdictions. Illinois Democrats argued federal officials have overstated risks. Border Czar Tom Homan praised states expanding detention capacity, noting that DHS is planning 1,000 more beds in Speedway, Indiana. Homan said, “Every bed we fill pretty quickly.” David Wilson covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
